findings.text: The assertion compares share["worker_slots"] against obligations._published_worker_slots(SESSION), the very function the view delegates to, so both sides read the same fixture document and move together: if that function regressed, the assertion would still pass. The independent literal beside it at line 89 (== SESSION_WORKER_SLOTS) is the assertion that actually guards the number; this line guards only that the view still delegates, and should say so or be dropped. Repeated at lines 138-140.

The block re-implements lane-document file reading (json.loads plus a try/except around read_text) instead of calling lane_document.read_lane_document_file, which the same module already uses at reckon/mcp_views.py:708 for the identical job and owns the unreadable-path handling. Two parses of one file can drift in their failure detail.

The per-session admission-row lookup is copied verbatim from reckon/crew/obligations.py:886-889 (same component for the row, same sessions_present gate, same UNKNOWN fallback). The row lookup is the lane_document/obligations owner's capability and should be asked of it rather than restated here.
